question: How Do I Cancel a Subscription Now Instead of at Period End?
metaDescription: The default customer-facing cancel keeps access until the paid period ends — here's how to force an immediate cancellation from the admin side instead.
shortAnswer: The customer-facing "Cancel" action always defers to the end of the current paid period by design. For a genuinely immediate cancellation — ending access right now regardless of what's already been paid for — an admin needs to change the subscription's status directly to "Cancelled" from the WooCommerce admin screen, rather than relying on the customer-facing cancel flow, and separately decide whether a partial refund for the unused remainder is appropriate.

bodyHtml:
How It Works

WooCommerce Subscriptions' standard cancellation flow moves a subscription to "Pending Cancellation" until the current billing period actually ends, then to "Cancelled" — this matches how most subscription billing is expected to behave (you don't lose access to something you already paid for). There's no customer-facing toggle for "cancel and lose access right now instead."

Why an Immediate Cancellation Is Sometimes Needed

  • A policy or legal requirement to stop billing and access immediately upon request in certain circumstances, rather than waiting for the period to lapse naturally.
  • A fraudulent or disputed order where continuing access even briefly isn't appropriate.
  • A customer service exception granted for a specific case, separate from the store's general cancellation policy.

How to Do It

  1. From the subscription's admin screen, change its status directly to "Cancelled" rather than going through the customer-facing flow — this stops future renewals immediately.
  2. Separately revoke access if it's tied to a status other than the subscription's own (a Memberships plan, a custom role, a third-party integration) — cancelling the subscription record doesn't automatically guarantee every connected system reacts instantly, so verify directly.
  3. Decide on a refund for the unused remainder of the current period, if that's the store's policy for this kind of exception, and process it as a separate action.
  4. For a store that wants immediate cancellation as the standard, customer-facing default rather than an admin exception, that's a deliberate business-policy change needing custom development to override the plugin's default end-of-period behavior for everyone.

See custom WooCommerce development if immediate cancellation needs to be a standard, self-service option rather than a manual admin exception.
